videos.postText: JEV IS INSANE your coding agents forget everything the second the session ends. Every fix. Every dead end you already hit. Every "no, not like that." Gone. Tomorrow you teach it all over again. Someone just open sourced the fix, and it runs on Jev. It's called Beacon, by @asymptotelabs. It pulls in your session history from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 20+ other agent tools and turns it into one shared memory. But storing everything isn't the hard part. Most agent runs are GARBAGE to learn from. Failed commands. Wrong turns. One off hacks you'd never want repeated. Save all of that and your agent just gets confidently worse. So Beacon keeps the full history, and Jev decides what actually earns a spot in memory. Promote it. Send it for review. Or throw it away. That's a decision you need on thousands of sessions, which is exactly why it has to be cheap. The runs that survive get turned into reusable skills. So something Cursor figured out on Monday shows up in your Claude Code session on Tuesday. Your agents stop starting from zero. Every good run makes the next one smarter. Repo: Star it and save this. follow @cyrilXBT

videos.postText: CÓ MỘT DEMO ĐANG LAN TRUYỀN TRÊN X VỀ JEV. Matthew Berman thử nghiệm và Jev xử lý 724 quảng cáo trực tiếp từ 37 thương hiệu chỉ trong 40 giây. Tổng cộng hơn 8.700 phân loại riêng lẻ mà chi phí token chỉ 0.09 đô. Nhiều người thắc mắc vì Jev vốn là mô hình phân loại văn bản có cấu trúc, không nhận trực tiếp tensor hình ảnh. Berman giải thích trong phần trả lời rằng pipeline phía trước dùng Gemini kèm embeddings để trích xuất token hình ảnh và văn bản thô. Sau đó dữ liệu này được đưa vào API của Jev để đánh giá song song các mục tiêu schema đã định sẵn như Choice, Score, Noul. Khác với cách sinh tự hồi quy truyền thống vốn dự đoán từng token một, Jev lấy mẫu toàn bộ quyết định schema trong một lượt lan truyền duy nhất. Nhờ vậy nó loại bỏ độ trễ tuần tự và đạt trung vị chỉ 216ms mỗi bản ghi. Điểm hay là không cần huấn luyện riêng đầu phân loại kiểu BERT hay DeBERTa, nó chạy được ngay với mọi định nghĩa schema tùy ý. Nhưng cần nhớ nó hoạt động trong cửa sổ ngữ cảnh 32k và không có bộ nhớ lâu dài. Nghĩa là đừng trông vào nó cho suy luận nhiều bước phức tạp hay các tác vụ cần ngữ cảnh tổ chức sâu. Nó giống một bộ định tuyến có điều kiện thông minh hơn là một agent tự trị. Vẫn là một primitive rất gọn để giảm code keo và đẩy bớt việc phân loại cơ bản ra khỏi các mô hình biên. Miễn là bạn giữ nó trong đúng ranh giới thiết kế thật sự.

videos.postText: Most AI automation breaks at the same spot: the decision. We are introducing world's first evaluation agent to work on automations alongside chat agents. An email comes in. Is it billing, access, or something else? A deal lands. Fast-track it, or hold it for review? A lead signs up. Worth a rep's time? Today most agents make that call and act on it in one opaque step. They write the reply, update the CRM, and call the tool. When they get it wrong, you can't see why, and you can't stop it. So today we're launching something different in Ballet: the evaluation agent. It's a new kind of agent. It doesn't act. It decides. It reads one record and returns one answer: → a choice (billing, access, or other) → a score (this lead is a 4 of 5) → or a probability (0.91 that this is a refund request) That answer comes with a confidence level. Your playbook branches on it, and a later step does the work. The reply, the CRM update and the handoff to a person all stay in steps you can see and control. Built on RLCD (reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions) using @typesafeai. Where teams are using it: • Triage a support email into the right queue • Route a deal review: fast-track, review, or hold • Score and route a lead • Catch a refund request before it becomes a churn risk • Check the work before a reply goes out Why this matters: automation you can trust starts with a decision you can inspect. When the decision is separate from the action, every run shows what was decided and how sure the agent was. You know exactly where a person should step in. The first 50 sign-ups get $100 in Ballet platform credits. Try it now →

videos.postText: Introducing Contrastive Language Model (CLM): an ultra-fast System One Model trained with a contrastive learning objective that connects states and actions. CLM-8B is pre-trained on internet-scale data and delivers up to 9× faster inference than Jev ⚡ while achieving comparable performance across computer-use, gaming, and tool-calling tasks. With lightweight fine-tuning, CLM-8B sets a new SOTA on challenging agentic coding benchmarks, such as DeepSWE (81.6%) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (87.6%). In contrast, Jev fails to serve as an effective verifier for these long-horizon tasks. We also build an efficient training and serving infra for CLMs by disaggregating states and actions, allowing their embeddings to be cached and reused independently. This substantially reduces inference latency in settings where the state evolves continuously while the action set remains fixed. Finally, we establish scaling laws for CLMs and show that the test contrastive loss decreases predictably as a power law in training compute, model size, and dataset size. 📄 Blog: 💻 Code: 🗣️ Discord: 🤗 Data & Models: More details on CLM’s architecture, data recipe, and scaling laws in the thread below 🧵

So I built one using Sai @sai_borg leveraging @typesafeai - Pretrained a few skills/move to play the game in Sai, including the special move - Sai navigates to start the game and decides which character he is most comfortable playing - Jev decides the best move to make almost simultaneously - Uses special moves when they’re ready - e.g. once enough energy has accumulated - Lost the first match, learned from the it, and won the second one 0 speed up the part when Sai is playing the game If you want to watch a computer use agent plays the game itself, try #robosecretary #SaiFleet

videos.postText: LLMs and Jev work very differently 😳 the simple version: LLMs generate text step by step Jev looks at the same context and returns structured decisions directly, with probabilities and confidence for example, a support ticket can ask: - is it urgent? - which team should handle it? - is the action risky? - is the task complete? with Jev, these decisions can be evaluated in parallel 3 main types: 1. Choice → pick an option 2. Score → rate something on a scale 3. Noul → yes/no with probability > 91% confidence → automate > 52% confidence → review or use a stronger model Jev isn't meant to replace LLMs it fits where your software already knows what decisions it needs to make 👀

videos.postText: ASTRA + JEV = CABBAGE I used GPT-6 Astra to build a trading desk. Then I gave Jev every decision. 21.6 seconds. $0.37 in API. 52,110 decisions. Astra built 3 bots: MACD momentum, RSI + VWAP reversal, CVD divergence. Wrote the code, the backtest and the risk manager. 1,200 configs went through the walk-forward backtest. 1,186 died. 14 survived all regimes. Then Cabbage started reading Robinhood Chain: > READS every fill, 20 seconds behind the block > ZEROES fake smart-money buys. 1 in 11 is fake > SCORES 536 wallets 0 to 100. Only 12 are worth copying > ASKS JEV when trusted wallets pile into one coin: BUY, HOLD or SELL? > WAITS if confidence is under 0.80 > ENTERS with a $100 ticket and a hard stop-loss the AI can't move > POSTS every call to Telegram instantly, to X an hour later Why two models: Astra thinks, writes, explains. Perfect for building. Jev answers one word in 0.1 seconds. Perfect for the moment money moves. A human reading the same data: 7h 14m. Cabbage: 21.6 seconds. Follow to see which Cabbage bot wins 🥬↓

videos.postText: today, i'm excited to share an early preview of the @avec desktop app, which is now rolling out in alpha to folks enrolled in avec's early access program. 5 months ago we released @avec to the app store. we started with a mobile app because it was clear to us that we could build something far better than the status quo there. but as we heard feedback from early users, we realized that there was a much bigger opportunity to do something special on desktop than we initially thought. desktop is not just a bigger screen: it's where you deal with your most important tasks, typically the ones you defer from mobile. what should the interface be when ai can do most of the pre-work for you so you can deal with what remains in a simpler, more focused interface? this demo covers some of the features of avec (e.g. the best prioritization of any email app, stack-based triaging, voice composition), but there are countless more that avec users love and we didn't have time to feature in this demo (e.g. our notifications that are so good you don't need to open the app to know what an urgent email is about, unsubscribe that actually works, or our 1-minute "clean your backlog" flow). one of the things that is most unusual about avec is how simple it is to use, yet how sophisticated it is behind the scenes. we built a 99.99% uptime email processing pipeline that pushes emails through a suite of llms to enrich them and delivers them to you within 10 seconds without ever losing one. we built a cross-device sync system similar to @linear's. we use a dozen or so different llms, and jev, leveraging robust evals and our taste to figure out which one fits for what application. check out the video (or the in-thread clips)! and in the spirit of lifting the veil, today only, ask your questions on how things work and i'll happily answer them here 👇 0:00 Introducing Avec for desktop 0:34 A quick tour of Avec on iPhone 2:05 Why we built a desktop app 2:45 Triaging emails on desktop 3:20 Core interactions: Done, Todo, Voice 3:57 Swipe through email with your trackpad 4:38 Instant sync between phone and desktop 5:34 Todos and keeping track of replies 6:15 A fast, context-aware AI sidebar 7:58 Automatic deadlines and rescheduling 8:45 Teaching Avec what matters to you 9:30 Review and clear low-importance emails 10:08 Desktop alpha rollout 10:49 How get early access

videos.postText: Kev puts Jev in front of an Obsidian vault and Claude Code answers a question about a CSV before he finishes typing it - the whole setup takes about three minutes. this is his follow-up tutorial, and the trick is that Jev never writes anything. it only decides which note, file or asset is the right one, then Claude Code does the work. community plugin on → MCP server enabled → API key handed to the agent → the vault becomes searchable memory → "we got it back before I even finished the sentence." "38% of medium rare steak eaters also do speed when they drive." - the answer that came out of a survey CSV he dumped into the vault the part that got me is what a vault actually is: a folder of markdown files. no index to build, no embeddings to maintain, and a logo search in the demo returns four files ready to drop into an editor. Jev is TypeSafe's System One model, so it costs a fraction of a cent per decision and answers in about a tenth of a second. the retrieval step stops burning tokens, because the model doing it isn't reading your whole repo. bookmark & watch today ↓

videos.postText: I just built a Jev Market Intelligence terminal. 18 models. 42 market data streams. 5,500 decisions per second. Most financial AI tools generate another paragraph about the market. This one turns millions of observations into one risk-adjusted view. • market analysis is the perfect Jev job: it is not writing - it is a battery of typed decisions: > is momentum strengthening or fading > is news sentiment confirming the move > is earnings quality improving > is options flow bullish or defensive > is the market regime expanding or contracting > is the trade crowded > how quickly will the signal decay classification and probability, not another market summary. • what the system analyses: > live prices across stocks and indices > 2.8M cross-asset observations > 12,480 financial headlines > momentum across 18 horizons > volatility regime and macro alignment > options-flow and order-book imbalance > correlations, liquidity and crowding risk every model evaluates one part of the market, then Jev combines the answers into a single conviction score with confidence and estimated signal half-life. • what you are watching: the left side is the live asset universe. the center reconstructs the selected stock through price, news, earnings, volatility, options and macro signals. the right side turns everything into the final output: Broadcom → 76/100 constructive confidence → 88.4% expected alpha → +1.82% signal half-life → 18.4 hours it does not replace the trading strategy. it decides whether the current market state is strong enough, clean enough and liquid enough for the strategy to act. market data → 18 signal models → Jev synthesis → conviction → risk-adjusted decision should I turn this into a public market intelligence tool? watch the full terminal run below ↓

videos.postText: Launching JevX — because AI shouldn’t tell you to use Jev everywhere. Though, I got early access to TypeSafe/Jev, and spent the last 5 days trying to answer a deceptively hard question: where does Jev actually belong in a real codebase? - After several failed approaches, pattern experiments, datasets, and studying and training with 44 open-source projects, After 4 versions, JevX v0.4.0 is the result — a tool that analyzes your codebase, finds places where deterministic rules may actually be making semantic decisions, and evaluates whether Jev is a good fit. JevX combines learned patterns, code structure, AI reasoning, and TypeSafe/Jev validation to produce a fit score instead of blindly suggesting Jev everywhere. The default cutoff is 70%, but you can change the threshold depending on how aggressive you want the analysis to be. The goal is simple: find where Jev should be used — and equally importantly, where it shouldn't. JevX 0.4.0 is now public. npm i -g @vij-sameerb5/jevx Not just a terminal CLI. ⚡ Run it instantly with npx @vij-sameerb5/jevx 🧣 Use it directly through MCP with Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini & Codex. This is Still building- not 100% correct, It’s open source. If you find an issue, have an idea, or want to build on it — open an issue or PR on GitHub. @typesafeai @karpathy @alexalbert__ @mattshumer_

videos.postText: HOLY SH*T JEV + JUPITER TRADING PANEL I haven't slept properly in a week and I don't even care. I think I just found the most unfair edge in memecoins right now, and almost nobody is using it yet. Here's the thing no one tells you: your bot doesn't lose because it's dumb. It loses because it's LATE. By the time a chat model finishes explaining why a token looks good, the pump is already over and you're exit liquidity. So I stopped asking AI to write essays and started asking it questions. Jev answers 4 of them in under 100ms: → is this real buying or fake noise? → are these wallets working together? → is the pump running out of gas? → how strong is this setup, 0 to 3? Then Jupiter takes over. It pulls a fresh quote, splits the order across 3 pools and fills before most bots have even parsed their first response. Watch the panel. It says NO way more often than it says yes. It skips coordinated pumps, it throws away late answers, and it walks away when the price moves. That's the whole secret: the trades you don't take matter as much as the ones you do. And the best part? Jev never touches my keys. It thinks, and the executor acts. I genuinely believe most traders are still going to be refreshing charts manually a year from now while bots like this eat the whole market.

videos.postText: I turned my Rubric eval platform into a small decision-model lab. Added Jev and started comparing it with chat LLMs on the same structured decisions. First run: Jev hit 100% accuracy, matching GPT-4o-mini, while showing 2.3× lower p50 latency (1.02s vs 2.39s) and 2× lower cost/1K. Then I put Jev into an actual routing pipeline instead of testing it in isolation, query → Jev → RAG / small LLM / big LLM / human, instead of throwing every query at the same model. Interesting part: the handwritten rules router got 100% route accuracy with 0 wrong routes, while Jev got 93.8% with 1 wrong route. Jev was also slower here (3.17s p50) and slightly more expensive. So yeah, Jev is fast + accurate, but deterministic rules still have their place. Still experimenting. Next up: Laya. The AI-model race is moving way too fast, so I’m trying to keep up and test these things on actual scenarios, not just benchmarks👀

ZERO LINES OF CODE COPIED jev opened the api four days ago. everyone rushed to build demos. i opened every repo and asked one question: what pattern here makes money a mario bot taught me to never parse screenshots. read structured state directly. my pool scanner reads chain state as json. no ui. no ocr. no guessing a drone controller taught me to put safety below the brain. deterministic checks fire before jev sees the pool. the model does not decide if a token is a honeypot. code does. for free an fps agent taught me to ask four questions per call instead of one. liquidity, team, narrative, timing. one request. four typed scores. 190ms a market maker on monad taught me that 81ms model latency exists. i benchmarked my pipeline at 190ms per pool. not hft. but faster than any agent framework chaining prompts a training data filter taught me to screen tokens the same way you screen training rows. description, twitter, telegram, creator wallet. garbage in, money out. unless you filter first a startup killer taught me to output three words: KILL, FIX, SHIP. my scoring matrix does the same. pass or skip. no appeals. no maybes the repo that made the biggest difference: an agent that prevents coding bots from lying about being done. i turned that into an adversarial checker. gets everything the other nodes wrote and looks for reasons NOT to buy ten repos. ten patterns. ten ideas i would never have had staring at my own code tuesday night the pipeline ran. 200+ pools entered. the adversarial checker killed most of them. three survived. one printed 1 ETH. not from a model. from reading other people's architecture and asking what if this was a trade full breakdown of every repo, every pattern, every mapping: article below

number that is exactly what a memecoin feed needs > agent-desktop reads the accessibility tree and picks the next button took: read the structure, not the picture. the village reads pool state, never a chart image > typesafe-mario plays mario from emulator ram, no screenshots took: the raw state is always cheaper than a rendering of it. detectors read reserves, not candles > jev-drone handles the high level while flight control keeps it stable took: jev decides, the engine executes. exits are never routed through the model > OneVOneJev judges movement, aim and fire every tick in a browser fps took: a decision per tick, not per minute. the village scores every launch the second it lands > jev-trader market makes on monad testnet at 81ms latency took: latency is the feature. jev scores a pool in 190ms before any agent spends a call > Prism judges toxic flow and mean reversion, then hands off to the strategy took: the filter and the trader are separate. jev sits in front, the agents stay untouched > neo4jev walks a knowledge graph edge by edge took: wallets are a graph. the spider now walks funder edges the same way > jev-curate screens training data before it enters a run took: videos.postText: JEV OPENED THE API. EVERYONE RUSHED TO BUILD DEMOS. I TOOK THE 10 BEST REPOS AND WIRED THEM INTO A TRADING PIPELINE. repo: did not copy a single line of code. pulled one architectural idea from each repo and mapped it to nerve. agent-desktop reads the desktop accessibility tree and decides where to click. i took the pattern of reading structured state instead of screenshots. pool scanner reads pool state directly from chain, no ui parsing. typesafe-mario plays mario without screenshots. reads emulator ram, gets structure, decides. same principle: typed state in, typed decision out. jev in nerve gets pool json and returns verdict json. no text. jev-drone controls a drone. stabilization and safety below, jev makes decisions above. in nerve this is the reflex layer. deterministic checks (bundle, sniper, honeypot) fire before jev even sees the pool. safety does not wait for the model. OneVOneJev plays an fps. every tick: movement, aim, fire, jump. four decisions per call. in nerve jev answers four typed questions per request: liquidity, team, narrative, timing. one call, four scores. 190ms. jev-trader market makes on monad testnet. model latency 81ms. i benchmarked nerve on solana: 190ms per pool. not hft, but faster than any agent framework chaining prompts. prism does not place orders itself. identifies state (toxic flow, mean reversion, pressure) and hands off to the strategy. nerve works the same way. jev does not trade. jev scores. the decision to buy is made by the user or the executor node. neo4jev stuffs jev into a knowledge graph. at each node decides which edge to take. in nerve this is the narrative map. grok builds a narrative graph from ct, jev decides which narrative is accelerating, which is dead. jev-curate filters training data. checks quality, relevance, risk of each row before letting it into the next training round. in nerve the memecoin analyzer does the same thing with tokens. description, twitter, telegram, whois, creator wallet history. filter before entry. canny prevents coding agents from lying about being done. looks at outputs, diffs, tests and judges whether to believe them. in nerve this is the adversarial checker. gets everything the other nodes wrote and looks for reasons not to buy. told to be harsh. killmyidea scores startups from multiple angles and outputs KILL, FIX or SHIP. the scoring matrix in nerve does the same thing. collects scores from all nodes, weighs them, outputs pass or skip. no appeals. 10 repos. 10 patterns. zero lines copied. architectural ideas only, mapped to trading. the best way to learn to code on a new model is to break down what others already built and apply it to your own problem.

videos.postText: Yesterday I assembled the tracks on MOSS, my open-source litter-picking robot running @dimensionalos. It rolled for the first time! Jev looks promising in simulation, but I can’t wait to test the full loop on the real robot: detection → decision → actuation. Assembly revealed plenty of room for improvement. I’ll keep building and testing this prototype over the next few days, simplifying the design, choosing components better suited to the job, and trimming the BOM cost wherever I can. The really cool part? I can document changes as I go and hand them to Codex to work on the next version while I keep building. Here’s the V0.4 animation. We’re getting close to releasing the CAD files and BOM so you can start building yours. Build, break things, iterate. Now in parallel.

videos.postText: GrokBot + Jev is the first trading agent setup I'd actually let near my account Most trading bots don't blow up on bad entries. They blow up after 3 losses, when they size up and revenge-trade. Mine did. So I split it: GrokBot does the analysis, Jev makes the calls it shouldn't make alone. setup took me 7 minutes: prompt → GrokBot → Jev decides → GrokBot executes → you confirm the order step 1 → get an API key at @typesafeai (never paste it in chat) step 2 → tell GrokBot: save it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY in the secure field step 3 → have GrokBot install typesafe-sdk on Agent Computer + smoke test system_one step 4 → write your risk rules into config: max 1% per trade, 3x leverage cap, 3-loss cooldown step 5 → add the jev-usage-router skill: before any order / resize / re-entry → ask the router, follow its action step 6 → run in shadow mode on paper first, read the logs - kill switch: enabled: false step 7 → go live: Jev decides, GrokBot executes, you confirm every order the result: 3 runs in the video - 3 losses in a row → cooldown 4h, drawdown -3.2% vs -18% without it - 0.6 BTC at 5x → resized to 0.059 BTC, risk capped at 1% - 8 tickers scanned → top 3 ranked, 0 orders sent the sizing rule doing the heavy lifting: size = (equity × risk%) / stop distance The LLM should read the market. It shouldn't be the one deciding when to stop.

videos.postText: Most enterprise AI doesn’t need to write an essay. It just needs to make a decision. Using an autoregressive LLM to route a ticket or check compliance is slow, expensive, and prone to hallucinations. TypeSafe AI’s Jev is the architectural fork we've been waiting for: System 1 Models. Why it matters: Fast & Cheap: Parallel sampling delivers strictly typed decisions in 70–500ms at $0.042/MTok (outputs are free). Zero Hallucinations: Schema-matching is guaranteed by design. No string parsing errors. Calibrated Confidence (RLCD): Every answer includes an honest probability score, allowing you to auto-run high-confidence paths and escalate only the ambiguous edge cases to expensive frontier LLMs. Runtime Flexibility: Logic lives in the schema, not the weights. Change your rules without retraining. The future of agentic architecture isn't one giant model doing everything. It’s System 1 (Jev) for millisecond decision pipelines + System 2 (Frontier LLMs) reserved for deep reasoning. Find the link in comments for full release and use cases..

videos.postText: Most of the AI we use is built for a person to talk to. What changes when software is the user? In a podcast this week, Diogo Almeida explains why Jev, the new System One model from TypeSafe AI is designed for code to consume its output. But what does that mean? I keep coming back to the spreadsheet analogy. Think of each Jev call as a cell: a small, cheap decision whose result can feed into other cells. A spreadsheet cell does very little on its own. Wire thousands together and you can model an entire business. Now imagine those cells can make judgments. Does this document contain the information we need? Do these two records refer to the same company? Which queue should this case go into? Code combines the answers into a larger workflow. What makes Jev so good at this type of work? It uses post-training process called RLCD which stands for Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions. The aim is to train a model to make useful decisions and represent its uncertainty honestly. If it assigns an outcome an 80% probability across comparable cases, that outcome should happen roughly 80% of the time. That gives software something to work with: thresholds for acting, gathering more evidence, or asking a person to review. You still need to test those thresholds on your own cases. Diogo's focus on “intelligence per dollar” feels especially practical here. Frontier benchmark scores tell us something about capability. When I'm building a workflow, I also want to know how much useful work we can do at a cost and error rate we can live with. There are so many small decisions we never automate because the economics don't make sense. Make those decisions cheap enough, calibrated enough, and easy to combine, and I think we could see a Cambrian explosion of new automation. Whole workflows assembled from steps that barely seemed worth building individually. That's the possibility I'm excited about. That's we're using Jev in the new AgentRun harness on (YC F26). By using it to route decisions in a workflow driven harness we can cut token consumption by up to 90% while improving accuracy! Jev is available in Grep's agent harness, too.

videos.postText: I have a confession. My Mac is a mess. So I built Sift, an open-source macOS app that looks at the files already sitting on your Mac and turns them into a searchable visual catalog. And you can install it directly from the link below. It catalogs your photos, screenshots, videos and documents where they already are, and lets you search for them the way you actually remember them. Often like: “that screenshot with the red chart”, “the photo from the restaurant”, or “that PDF about that school project”. It can also find duplicates and suggest where things should go, but nothing moves until you approve it. Most of the work happens directly on the Mac. And yes, apparently I needed to build an AI app to finally deal with my Downloads folder. I also used Jev from @typesafeai for some of the small decisions inside Sift, where using a giant model would make absolutely no sense. videos.postText: JEV RUNS IN THE CLOUD. LAYA-MLX PLAYS SNAKE 60 TIMES A SECOND ON YOUR LAPTOP. I ported Laya to MLX and pushed the inference loop until it fit inside 1 GB of memory. It now runs locally on an M3 Max. No server. No API calls. No waiting for a remote model to answer. Laya is a lightweight classification system built around text output probabilities. The video shows the result: a model making 60 game decisions per second while playing Snake on-device. That makes it roughly 50x faster than Jev in the same kind of loop. The interesting part is not Snake. It is what happens when a model this small can read a state, classify it and act before a cloud agent has finished responding.

videos.postText: NVIDIA released a fast speaker-labeling model today: Nemotron 3 Diarization. Like all of the Nemotron family from @NVIDIA_AI, this is an open weights model, so you can grab the weights from @huggingface and use the model in the cloud or on your local device. Nemotron 3 Diarization is a useful building block for voice agents and realtime AI applications that need to handle speech from multiple people at the same time. It handles overlapping speech well, can identify up to eight speakers, and pairs with any transcription model you're using in your multi-modal pipelines. @jonptaylor built a demo (code below) and recorded a technical deep-dive showing how to use this diarization model together with a speech-to-text model. Jon's code also uses Jev for super-accurate confirmation of critical voice input in a noisy/multi-speaker environment.

videos.postText: JEV does not make an AI agent faster by magic the real speed comes from removing unnecessary thinking from decisions the system makes over and over again. formula: Faster Agent Loop = Structured State + JEV Decision Layer + Smart Routing + Verification 8% -> define the task. Separate the real objective from all the extra context around it. 21% -> isolate repeated decisions. Things like “which tool?”, “retry or stop?”, “is this valid?”, and “what happens next?” 43% -> move those decisions into JEV. Give it structured state, exact criteria, and a small set of possible outcomes. 68% -> route execution intelligently. Easy decisions stay inside the fast path. Hard or uncertain cases fall back to the stronger model. 84% -> verify every important output. Failed checks loop back into the system before they become real actions. 100% -> update memory and run the next cycle. The loop gets cleaner because every decision, route, and result becomes part of the next state. JEV handles the repeated decisions. The larger model handles ambiguity and complex reasoning. Verification keeps bad routes from propagating through the system. I visualized the full JEV Engineering loop below ↓

videos.postText: I just built a Jev X Swarm Controller and put 300 agents on autopilot for 6 minutes. 300 K3 workers on autopilot. 6 minutes. 12,480 turns. Jev made a decision on every one of them. 91 reached me. A swarm knows how to execute. It does not know when to stop. every turn gets 6 typed questions: is this result good enough, is there new information, is this the same state as last turn. then one action: continue / retry / stop / merge / spawn / escalate. what the loop actually did: 1,642 STOP - same state twice, the loop was going nowhere 806 MERGE - two workers on the identical finding 91 ESCALATE - irreversible or out of policy, so a human decides without it, 41 workers would still be running right now. 3,208 wasted turns avoided. $2.12 for all 12,480 decisions. 0.17 ms each. the swarm is not the hard part. the stopping is. Read this article on Jev Engineering below and turn your ideas into reality.

videos.postText: JEV CHECKS IF YOUR HOTEL IS LYING I built a terminal that takes every claim made by a vacation hotel in its description - first line, sea view, quiet, recently renovated and cross-checked it against guest reviews. For every claim made by a hotel one verdict and a confidence score in percent. Here is the picture that emerged, Jev checked 40 hotels in Antalya, and only one was left that meets the conditions and it happens to be one of the cheapest. Jev calibrated the hotels, two exaggerations the hotel is eliminated. Then it checked for one exaggeration, and those that failed were eliminated as well. The terminal shows precisely how the hotel verification against guest reviews works.

videos.postText: You can now just tell Jev what you want. Press Cmd K on and type it the way you would say it. The search box turns your sentence into a card that does it: "bonded under 100k mc" becomes a screen. Jev reads your filters out of the sentence, shows how many coins match and the first five, and one press opens the full list. "is solana:DezXAZ8z7PnrnRJjz3wXBoRgixCa6xjnB7YaB1pPB263 safe" becomes a check. Jev finds the coin and gives its read: skip, watch or bid, the risk, and whether buyers are in control. "track wif" becomes a track. One press and Jev watches the coin for you and pings you when its call on it changes. The model only picks which of the three cards you meant, and the corner of the card shows how sure it is. Every filter and every number on the card comes from what you typed and from live market data, never made up by the model. Enter runs the card. Want a different one? Click it.

videos.postText: 卧槽？？一个不到 2B、能本地部署的小模型，给真实 Issue 做分类，跟 JEV 的结果居然这么接近？ 最近 JEV 的玩法看了不少，给邮件分类、给 Agent 选工具。这类需求太常见了，我就想知道这张工单该分给谁、下一步该调用哪个工具，真不用每次都给我写一篇分析。 所以这次我把 JEV 和 This That 都接进 Pi，直接拉了 OpenAI Codex 仓库的 30 条真实 Issue，让它们现场做题。 用户是在报 Bug、提功能需求，还是问怎么用？问题出在登录、界面、执行还是会话？ 同一份内容、同一组选项，每条做两项判断，两边各发 60 次请求。 跑完一看：JEV 用了 23.5 秒，This That 用了 25.6 秒。30 条里，28 条的两项判断完全一样，两边都没出现请求失败。 速度这轮还是 JEV 快一点。但 This That 只有 18.8 亿参数，权重约 3.76GB，而且能下载到自己机器上跑。这个结果真让我想继续折腾一下了。 它的用法也很干脆：把问题和选项给进去，一次计算直接返回选择和概率。程序拿到结果就能接着往下走，不用再从一大段回答里抠出一个“是”或者“否”。 更实用的是本地部署。客户工单、内部文档、还没发布的产品资料，这些东西只是想分个类，也不一定愿意全部发到外面的 API。 This That 支持 NVIDIA GPU、Apple Silicon 和 CPU，可以把这一步判断留在自己的设备上。做 Agent 的人，手里又多了一个能自己控制的小工具。 这次我跑的是 API 对比，本地性能还没测。28/30 是两个模型判断一致，也不等于准确率，这两个口径先说清楚。 完整录屏放上面。做客服分流、邮件分类、Agent 工具选择的，直接拿一批自己业务里的真实数据试试，比盯着榜单猜有用。 模型和权重： 免费体验地址：

videos.postText: JEV does not make an AI agent faster by magic the real speed comes from removing unnecessary thinking from decisions the system makes over and over again. formula: Faster Agent Loop = Structured State + JEV Decision Layer + Smart Routing + Verification 8% -> define the task. Separate the real objective from all the extra context around it. 21% -> isolate repeated decisions. Things like “which tool?”, “retry or stop?”, “is this valid?”, and “what happens next?” 43% -> move those decisions into JEV. Give it structured state, exact criteria, and a small set of possible outcomes. 68% -> route execution intelligently. Easy decisions stay inside the fast path. Hard or uncertain cases fall back to the stronger model. 84% -> verify every important output. Failed checks loop back into the system before they become real actions. 100% -> update memory and run the next cycle. The loop gets cleaner because every decision, route, and result becomes part of the next state. JEV handles the repeated decisions. The larger model handles ambiguity and complex reasoning. Verification keeps bad routes from propagating through the system. I visualized the full JEV Engineering loop below ↓

videos.postText: Jev is getting picked up everywhere right now. If you already have access to the Jev API but aren't sure what to point it at first, just copy this checklist. Ten decisions that pay off on day one, in the order I would wire them: 1. the loop exit Stop asking a frontier model "are we done" on every turn. One Noul, read against fresh tool output instead of the agent's own summary of it. 2. the model router A Choice over your tiers before work starts. Rename goes cheap, design change goes frontier, unclear goes to a person. 3. the merge gate Choice for the verdict, Score for how hard it is to undo, Noul for whether a human should read it. Three answers, one call, branch order in your code. 4. the command guard Allow, ask or block before anything runs. Deny rules sit first in code; Jev handles only what code cannot compute. 5. the relevance filter Score every tool output before it enters context. One public build took a session from roughly a million tokens down to 86K. 6. ticket triage Choice over departments, Score over urgency, Noul over "needs a human". Runs on every ticket, not on a sample. 7. the reranker Forty passages came back from retrieval. Score them against the question, keep the four that earn their tokens. 8. the live menu Offer only the buttons, workers and sources that exist right now. A dead option picked at 0.91 is still dead. 9. the content screen Split the draft into claims, one narrow Noul each, anything that trips goes to an editor. Nothing is rewritten automatically. 10. shadow mode Run all nine beside your current logic for a week, log what they would have done, then read your thresholds off your own curve. Copy these Jev blueprints - then read the full Jev setup below ↓ ↓

videos.postText: 🚨 THIS IS WHAT A “SECOND BRAIN” FOR AI AGENTS LOOKS LIKE. 𝗡𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗵𝗮 𝗞𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿 built Laya — a fast, non-autoregressive decision engine designed to make decisions instead of generating long answers. Instead of asking an LLM to explain everything, Laya returns the decision your software actually needs. → `choice` → pick between options → `score` → return an ordinal score → `noul` → probability for a yes/no proposition → Single forward pass → No text generation → Supports 100+ languages → Built-in Router chooses the appropriate checkpoint → Can run as a Jev-compatible HTTP API And the speed is wild: 32.8 ms for one multilingual decision on a T4 GPU. The really interesting part? Laya can be used for things like: routing → guardrails → moderation → support triage → agent decisions So instead of: state → giant LLM response → parse it you get: state → typed decision → action And yes, this project is directly positioned as a Jev-compatible alternative, while being open-source and Apache 2.0 licensed. 🔗 #Laya #Jev #AI #LLM #AIAgents #MachineLearning #OpenSource #Python #AIInfrastructure #Developers

videos.postText: An access ticket came in. Here's the workflow that closed it, step by step, with what each step cost.20 steps. 4 judgment calls go to @typesafeai 's Jev, not an LLM. The LLM runs once. Whole ticket: ₹0.16. Jev's share: under 1 paisa. What ran: 1. Code pulls the repo + ticket (free) 2. Jev triages: config change, 100% conf, 326 ms 3. LLM edits one line of config on a branch (30s, ~15 paise) 4. Jev reads the diff before the push: safe 95% 5. Code pushes, comments on the ticket 6. Spawns a monitor fot git and Jira The pattern: → code first, for anything with an algorithm → Jev for judgment: typed answers with a confidence, so routing is a rule, not a prompt → an LLM only where something must be written → hard budgets per run Routing is data: push_gate.safe.noul >= 0.7 → push The monitor is a workflow too: a cron, one check, two questions, ~40 paise a day. It reports back; the parent knows an update from a fresh ticket. Caveat for India: not all data can leave the country. Reflex routes per step, so sensitive steps can stay on an in-country model. Reflex is open source and very new. It WILL have bugs. Issues and PRs welcome, small ones included. Built on the Pi coding agent, any model via @OpenRouter , voice via @SarvamAI . MIT.

videos.postText: 看了@karminski3这个测试觉得很有趣 但是总觉得Jev能力不至于此，于是在这套框架基础上补充测试了多组结果，详见视频。 首先是对照组： C0 —— 这个就是牙医的整活随机算法，随机游走。 C1 —— 这个是专业的迷宫算法，类似机器人走迷宫比赛会用到的。 C2 —— 这个是让gpt-5.6-luna模仿类似方法，在同一个Session里一步步探索迷宫。 然后是实验组，全部都是基于Jev的方案： E0 —— 这个就是牙医的Jev, 的确卡死在一个局部���优里 E1 —— 这个是在牙医Jev的基础上，扩充了上下文，包括全部历史操作以及已观察到的地图 E2 —— 这个是把专业迷宫算法的思路，用自然语言告知了Jev，并提供了全部通道经过次数的统计 E3 —— 这个是在E1的基础上，优化了prompt，删除多处对剩余距离的强提示，转而让Jev自己思考最佳策略 简单总结一下结论： 1. 站在成功率和性能视角： 专业算法 > Jev+专业Knowhow > Jev + 通用思路 > LLM 2. Jev的主要价值： - Jev自带智能，如果你不具备解题最佳实践，Jev可以替代一部分专业算法； 如果你具备最佳实践, 不必再用代码实现它，直接告诉Jev就行； - Jev比LLM快且省 3. Jev需要更好的prompt engineering以及harness： - 对比E0 和 E1, 增加上下文能让Jev减少陷入局部最优 - 对比E1 和E3 ，减少对终点距离的强提示，把更多决策权交给Jev，貌似从根本上解决了局部最优问题 详见：

videos.postText: JEV passed every recent Vercel model launch within 12 hours. By hour 18, more than 10% of paid teams had already used it. At hour 24, adoption was near 13%, while every comparison launch remained below 7%. Those numbers made me test the product thesis against a harsher interface: an AI memecoin desk. This is a paper concept, not a live Jev integration. Eight Grok agents produce the research. The proposed $3,195 order is cut to $742 after liquidity and risk checks. JEV receives only the state required to choose the next branch. The feed expires at 11.5 seconds. JEV returns REJECT. FENCE blocks permission. The final order becomes $0 before anything reaches the simulated Robinhood boundary. The model's early adoption may fade. Vercel says that is the next real test. But the demand signal is already clear: developers want AI that can make small, structured decisions inside software without generating another page of text. That workload appears everywhere once you start looking for it.

videos.postText: Jev in the control plane is the first agent setup I have run without sitting behind it 99% of people put an LLM on every decision and pay 400x for an answer that takes 3 seconds. 1% run the decision layer separately. the whole shape is one line: prompt → orchestrator → Jev decision + p → toll booth → fast lane or human → tool → observations back 8 steps and the architecture is done: step 1 → log the action before you execute it, in the same DB transaction as the request. if the process dies, the action is still recorded. step 2 → put it on kafka partitioned by session_id. one agent session stays ordered, and you get replication and idempotency keys for free. step 3 → make the orchestrator stateless. plan, react, manage tool calls, track state. state lives in kafka and the execution log, never in the process. step 4 → send every decision to Jev, not to the LLM. route, classify, score, extract, branch. typed output, sampled in one parallel pass, 70 to 500 ms, $0.042 per million in and output free. call the LLM only when the answer genuinely needs strings. step 5 → build the toll booth: policy → authorisation → validation → idempotency. nothing reaches a tool without passing all four. this box needs 10K decisions a second, which is exactly why it cannot run on a model that takes 3 to 329 seconds. step 6 → use the calibrated probability as the gate. over the gate it runs in the fast lane. under the gate it goes to quarantine, a human sees the proposed action and the reasoning, and it is revalidated in full before it executes. approval never permanently bypasses policy. step 7 → never call external tools synchronously, and never blindly retry an ambiguous state changing action. idempotent outbox, then reconcile: safe → finalise, blocked → quarantine, unknown → human review. step 8 → run it in shadow for 20 to 50 real decisions. the agent works normally while every Jev route is logged next to what you would have done. promote only the routes that hold. you are done. the model was never the bottleneck. the decision layer was.

You watch it think with 0 capital at risk. 3 commands and it boots: cp .env.example .env bun install bun run start The numbers from the repo itself: ��� order book read, p50 18 ms → whole loop, p50 100 ms → exactly 2 RPC calls per block, 1 to read, 1 to send → nothing else on the hot path That last line is the part worth having. The low latency engine is the hard half, and it is sitting there finished under MIT. One thing every repost leaves out: with no TypeSafe key it does not run Jev at all. videos.postText: Jev要被开源模型干掉了 ？我来实测两个决策模型的能力，到底有没有吹牛？ Jev 实际上不应该跟LLM相比，要测就得找同一个生态位的对手！于是我找到了同样是决策模型的 FLock——一个超轻量级的决策模型，而且完全开源免费 为了不测垃圾数据，我从美国消费者金融保护局（CFPB）公开数据库摘了 1,000 条真实的真人长篇控诉（包含真实口语、愤怒投诉、维权错字以及乱码垃圾单），同时喂给这两个主打毫秒级决策的模型，实时分流到 15 个细分金融业务部门👇 左边：TypeSafe Jev（jev-latest） 右边：FLock（this-that-model-1.0）（开源免费） ─── 具体正确率表现如下 ─── • 日常核心业务 │ Jev: 90%~95% │ FLock: 85%~98% （双方差距不大） • 复杂长文过滤 │ Jev: 70%~100%│ FLock: 14%~61%（Jev占优） • 决策时间对比 │ Jev:33.5 S │ FLock: 36.1S （Jev占优） • API响应速度 │ Jev: 368ms │ FLock: 405ms （双方差距不大） • 官方API 成本 │ Jev: $0.146│ FLock: $0 （Flock成本完胜） ──────────────────────── 客观总结： Jev @typesafeai 在“复杂问题”表现更好： 只要你的业务涉及到多重逻辑交织的复杂长文本、严苛的垃圾噪音拦截、或是误判代价极高的核心环节，Jev 依然是定力最强的选择 FLock @flock_io 免费开源，日常场景性价比无敌： 在占了 80% 以上的高频日常场景里，FLock 准确率稳在 85%~98%，完全够用了，重点的是它仅 2B 参数且开源免费，太厉害了，目前FLock 接API限时免费 同时也可以本地部署 FLock，完全不吃电脑配置：底层仅2 B 参数，一张普通 3060 显卡甚至苹果 MacBook（原生支持 MPS）就能直接拉起来。在消费级显卡上，它的本地推理延迟最低只有 约 31 毫秒...还可以做本地 LoRA 微调...这是JEV没有的优势，太香了🧐@y95277777

videos.postText: an ai news desk that reads 9,000 items a month costs $25.60 to run. 60 cents of that is the ai. if you're building one and aren't sure which stages should touch a model, copy this checklist: 1. collect sources lab blogs, release notes, research feeds, permitted apis. keep the original link on every item or you cannot verify anything later. CODE. never a model. 2. build records headline, text, author, date, source id, url, collection time. a missing field stays missing, it does not get guessed. CODE. never a model. 3. exact filters freshness window, dead links, duplicate ids, normalised titles. a model is measurably worse at counting and comparing dates, so it never gets asked. CODE. drops 4,200 of 9,000. 4. bounded questions sort the topic, score the fit, flag a numeric claim. fixed answer set, generates nothing. JEV. 5. same event? cheap title similarity shortlists the pair, then one judgment on the two summaries. never run the model across the whole set. JEV. 4 and 5 together drop 4,440. 6. verify the claim benchmarks, cost reductions, adoption figures, checked against the original paper or filing. a flag is not a verification. HUMAN. drops 270. 7. write the draft source excerpts, confirmed facts, unresolved caveats, tone, format. stored next to its evidence record. LLM. the only stage that writes a sentence. 90 drafts, $0.22. 8. approve or kill the pipeline stops at draft ready for review. no confidence value overrides this. HUMAN. drops 26. 64 get posted. $0.38 jev + $0.22 llm + $25.00 for the feed = $25.60 a month. $0.28 per approved draft. 97.7% of that bill is access to the material. whatever this desk is limited by, it is not the price of inference. workflow from @Dain0x, arithmetic recomputed and it reproduces. copy this checklist, then read the full workflow below ↓

videos.postText: I gave Jev $30 and one line: "make it 500x or I shut you down" it didn't ask how. didn't ask for a strategy. didn't warn me about risk it just started reading $30 to $15,847.20 in 9 hours. paper session, every fill logged live I went to sleep. woke up, opened jevfun, and the number was already there here's what nobody gets about it: Jev isn't a bot that buys everything new on PUMPFUN Jev is a filter that happens to have a wallet every token that lands on PUMPFUN gets read. 150 at a time on one screen, one dot each, sliding toward graduation. a read line passes over the whole field every 3.4 seconds five agents read every token before Jev is allowed to want it > HOLDERS reads the top ten wallets and knows when three of them own the supply > DEV watches the creator wallet and flags the first sell > SNIPERS counts every wallet that bought in block zero > BUNDLES finds wallets funded from the same source > FLOW measures buy vs sell pressure over the last 30 seconds each one votes up or down. Jev scores it out of 100 below 55 it doesn't even look twice above 75 it buys DEV and BUNDLES can kill any entry at any score. a kill doesn't get appealed at hour two the balance dropped to $6.40 Jev went quiet. 312 tokens read, zero entries. everything came back AVOID. dev still holding 30%. four bundle clusters. sells 3x buys it didn't revenge-trade. it didn't lower the bar. it waited around hour four one token came back different top10 at 22%. dev at 1.4% and not selling. zero bundles. buys 2.4x sells JEV SCORE 91. STRONG. entry filled $6.40 to $38.90 in 11 minutes after that it just kept going. read, skip, skip, skip, enter. all night. no human input 1,946 tokens read. 41 entries. 58 rugs flagged and never touched a human doing this by hand checks one token in 20 minutes. videos.postText: jev + picsart turned one prompt into a creative system that decides before it spends instead of letting expensive models guess their way through every step, i split the workflow in two: Jev handles the cheap decisions, Picsart handles the actual generation. here’s exactly how i wired it: step 1 → the brief enters once. every image, clip, audio pass and edit inherits the same campaign direction instead of starting from a blank prompt. step 2 → Jev sits before the expensive work. it decides whether the next stage should run, stop, reuse something finished, or wait for me. step 3 → the decision set stays tiny: allow_subagent, ask_human, stop_retry, reuse_cache. cheap calls first, expensive generation second. step 4 → Picsart takes over the creative layer. 188 models from 34 providers sit behind the graph for image, video, audio and editing. step 5 → every job gets its own stage. one model does not have to carry the brief, image, motion, sound and final polish by itself. step 6 → when review rejects one output, Jev does not blindly request v2, v3, v4. it can stop the retry and change the route first. step 7 → approved work stays alive. reuse_cache can keep 5 finished stages untouched while only the 1 broken branch gets another run. step 8 → human review only appears where judgment matters. i am not approving every tiny action, just the decisions where taste can change the result. step 9 → the cost gap is the fun part: 11 Jev decisions cost $0.0011 here, versus roughly $0.33 through the heavier LLM decision loop. step 10 → once the graph works, the next campaign is not another rebuild. swap the brief, keep the logic, and run the same system again. jev decides what deserves compute. picsart turns that decision into the asset.

videos.postText: Jev has been blowing up lately. If you already have API access but don't know where to start, just copy this checklist: 1. jev-browser Drives a real headless browser through MCP, CLI or a library. Jev picks one action per step from the page's clickable and typeable elements, and scores whether the goal is met or the run is stuck. 2. jev-browser-agent Per-step browser decisions at about a second. One request asks "which operation" and "which target" together, and confidence under 0.6 escalates to a bigger model or to you. 3. typesafe-jev-bridge Zero-dependency OpenAI-compatible bridge. Use typed yes/no, choice and score judgments from Claude Code, Cursor, Cline or any OpenAI SDK, over CLI or HTTP. 4. pilot-typesafeai-jev Jev inside LangGraph and Deep Agents. One request asks three questions, plain code picks the route, and only the winning route spends chat model tokens. 5. building-with-jev-skill An agent skill for writing programs that call Jev: question design, state structure, thresholds, and how to diagnose a question that answers wrong. 6. jev-skill Guided setup plus evaluation workflows, with a read-only presence check and no silent provider switches or fabricated probabilities. 7. awesome-jev Source-backed catalogue of what people actually shipped, sorted by category, with limitations noted per entry. 8. awesome-typesafe-jev Field guide with SDKs, live demos, agent tools and independent evaluations, including where the vendor numbers came from. 9. awesome-jev-by-typesafe Evidence-backed use cases, patterns and starter code, with the 70 to 500 ms latency claim marked as vendor-reported. 10. awesome-jev (cobanov) The widest catalogue right now: SDKs in Go, Java and JS, MCP connectors, guardrail experiments and studies. descriptions.pt-br: Encaminhar decisões de parada, nova tentativa, fusão, criação e escalonamento de agentes em enxame com $0.042 reportados

videos.postText: Most AI agent swarms know how to execute. They don't know when to stop. That's the gap Jev Engineering's "Autopilot" is built to close. The problem: once you unleash a swarm of agents (like Kimi's, running up to 4,000 steps), every "should we keep going?" decision either gets routed back to the expensive frontier model or to a human and both are slow and costly. Meanwhile the API billing meter just keeps running. Jev's fix: pull those between-turn decisions out of the frontier-model loop entirely and hand them to a cheap, instant decision layer. The loop becomes simple Discover → Decide (Jev) → Execute (Kimi, in parallel, at scale) → Save → Repeat? Jev doesn't do the work. It makes the call on whether the work should continue navigate, stay on target, or call it finished. The number that makes the case: running 300 Kimi agents as a swarm, Jev's decision layer added up to $0.042 a rounding error next to what constant frontier-model check-ins would cost. The bigger point: intelligence and judgment are two different jobs. A muscle that never gets told when to stop isn't autonomy, it's just momentum. Where do you think the real risk sits with agent swarms the execution, or the missing "should we stop" layer?

videos.postText: JEV JUST TURNED THE HARDEST PART OF AI ENGINEERING INTO A MULTIPLE CHOICE TEST a model that cannot write code, cannot write prose, cannot reason - and that is exactly why it wins. six days ago somebody shipped 139,000 lines of Rust that does nothing but ask it ONE question: which skill loads next. 114 stars already. skillranker does not generate anything. it hands your live session to Jev as a typed Choice, gets back one option from a set it defined, plus a probability. the agent still decides what to consult. 5 rules before you wire it in. -> SEPARATE the deciding from the generating. "which skill fits this turn" is multiple choice with a bounded answer set. most loops burn a frontier generative call on it. two logical requests, at most four HTTP attempts, a three second total budget - that is the entire ranking path. -> DEMAND a real none-of-these. both comparison passes carry an explicit abstain option and the thing stays silent when nothing fits. a ranker that always ranks is a ranker that always interrupts. abstention shows up in 36 of its files - it is load bearing, not a flag. -> READ the limitations section before the benchmarks. this repo does that work for you: "these targets are not remote-service guarantees or measured benchmark results." a perf table that disclaims itself is worth more than one that does not. -> KEEP observations apart from judgments. it logs observed load, unobservable, censored, and explicit usefulness judgment as four different things, then says outright that load observations are affected by the suggestion itself. most agent telemetry collapses all of it into "it worked." -> ASSUME retrieval is the ceiling. past 254 skills a lexical prefilter narrows the set before Jev ever sees it, and the repo admits that step misses paraphrases. your ranker is only as good as the candidate list you handed it. third time this year the interesting engineering was in the abstain path and not the ranking would you let something rank your skills if it could not tell you it had nothing

videos.postText: We just open-sourced ai2human Onus: the first verification layer where the evidence can veto the model. A model will happily tell you a forged screenshot is real, with 0.99 confidence. Onus says no. Every piece of evidence gets a grade, E0–E4, by how hard it is to fake, and a low grade can never auto-approve, whatever the model says. You run a giveaway: "Reply to our post, get $1." Overnight: 1,000 replies. Half are "gm", ads, bots, copy-paste. An LLM review is slow and pricey. Doing it by hand takes all day. That is the gap Onus fills. One rule behind it: The burden of proof is on the evidence. 🧵 1. Evidence grades, not just scores E0–E4 by how hard the evidence is to fake. A screenshot never auto-passes, even at 0.99. That rule lives in code; the model cannot override it. 2. Code checks what code can Task code present? Duplicate? Empty claim? Code decides first. The model answers only what it is good at: does the content meet the requirement. 3. The model scores, code controls the money Judgment and payout are fully separated. The bar rises with the value at stake. 4. The weakest link decides Criteria combine by minimum, not average. A 0.95 "relevant" cannot hide a 0.2 "genuine". 5. Every verdict is replayable Each result ships a receipt: evidence grade, pinned model version, full probabilities, hash. 6. Measured on live Jev, not estimated 0.4s per check, ~$0.02 per 1,000, all 5 off-topic submissions caught. The one to look at: across 30 cases the model alone let 1 forgery through. With the grade gate, 0. That forgery scored 0.90. 7. No vendor lock-in Jev, open-source kev, or your own model, one setting. MCP-native, callable from Claude and Codex, batch mode built in. 8. Early, come break it Known limits are listed in the README. Fool it, tell me, and I will fix it and credit you publicly. If you know another project that grades evidence and lets it veto the model, reply with the link. I will credit you and add it to the README. Free and open source, MIT 👉 Star it if you want this to keep getting better. #Jev #AIAgents #MCP #OpenSource #BuildInPublic

videos.postText: YOU’RE PAYING FOR AI IN THE WRONG PLACES. The costliest mistake in the AI ​​business is forcing a powerful model to make every single decision. Filter. Evaluate. Select. Weed out. Route. You don’t always need the most expensive model for that. That’s why the Jev + DeepSeek + GPT + Claude combination looks so promising: a low-cost layer handles simple decisions, while expensive models kick in only where they truly add value. The same principle applies to content creation. Instead of juggling dozens of disjointed AI tools, there’s @Picsart - where 188 AI models and tools for generating and editing visual content are all gathered in one place. Less switching. Less wasted spend. More control over the entire AI pipeline. But the most interesting part is how to turn this architecture into a real, profitable AI business. Don’t just scroll past this article. Open it now and break down at least one of the five scenarios. That’s where you might find the next AI service you can launch. The model accepts the current state plus a set of questions across three types—Choice (selecting from options), Score (rating on a scale), and Noul (probability that a statement is true)—and returns ready-made answers, complete with probabilities and confidence levels, in tens to hundreds of milliseconds While such "micro-decisions" are found in almost every product, integrating them used to be costly, slow, or cumbersome. videos.postText: Laya just launched as an open-source alternative to Jev. Built by ConvAI Innovations, Laya is designed for fast decision tasks where you do not need a full LLM to generate text. Give it an email, support ticket, JSON payload, or plain text, and it can immediately return a label, score, or probability. Examples: ▪️ Is this email spam? ▪️ Which team should receive this ticket? ▪️ How urgent is this issue? ▪️ Is this a prompt injection attempt? ▪️ Should an agent take action or escalate? The key difference is that Laya does not generate text at all. You get a structured decision directly, so there is no need to parse an LLM response and extract JSON afterward. There are three versions: ▪️ English-focused ▪️ Multilingual with 100+ languages ▪️ Specialized for agents, support, invoices, and security alerts Model sizes range from 322M to 421M parameters. On a Tesla T4, the multilingual model reportedly handles a single request in about 32.8 ms and a batch of 10 in 72.3 ms. The authors claim roughly 7x higher speed than Jev, although the Jev numbers come from third-party tests, so it is not a direct apples-to-apples benchmark. The biggest advantage is openness. Laya is released under Apache 2.0, can run locally without an external API, and is available as a Python package. Project: GitHub: #AI #OpenSource #AIAgents

videos.postText: Jev 居然输给了一个 1.88B 本地模型？我用俄罗斯方块重新测了一遍 当我看到 this-that-model-1.0 在 68 道决策题上做到 94.1% 准确率，而 Jev 是 76.5% 时，我的第一反应是： 这是真的假的？ 一个只有 1.88B 参数、可以在 Mac 本地运行的小模型，真的能在决策任务上超过 Jev 吗？ 所以我做了一个俄罗斯方块，让两个模型使用相同的棋盘规则、随机种子和方块顺序。程序负责计算所有合法落点，模型只负责决定方块应该放在哪里。 1️⃣ 一开始，Jev 的表现更好 最初，我先过滤掉明显更差的落点，再把剩下的多个候选位置同时交给模型。 在这一模式下，Jev 的表现更加稳定。 我观察到的一轮里： Jev 消除了 5 行，this-that 消除了 3 行。 如果只看到这里，很容易得出结论：本地小模型还是不如 Jev。 但我后来意识到，这种问题可能并不是 this-that 最擅长的形式。 2️⃣ 换成“二选一”后，结果反了 this-that 本质上是一个 typed decision model，更擅长候选明确、边界清楚的选择题。 所以我把决策方式改成了淘汰赛： A 和 B，哪个落点更好？ 胜者进入下一轮，继续和其他候选位置比较，直到选出最终落点。 换成这种模式后，我观察到的一轮结果变成了： this-that 消除了 7 行，Jev 只消除了 1 行。 this-that 的棋盘也更加平整，留下的空洞更少。 模型没有变，游戏没有变。 唯一改变的，是我向模型提问的方式。 3️⃣ 这个模型特别在哪里？ this-that-model-1.0 只有约 18.8 亿参数，采用 MIT License，可以下载到本地运行。 它不写小作文，也不慢慢生成 Token。 你给它当前状态、一个问题和几个合法选项，它通过一次前向计算直接返回： 选择哪个 + 每个选项的概率 因此它很适合任务分流、Skill 选择、队列判断、风险分级，以及 Agent 下一步动作这类高频决策。 官方模型卡公布的 68 道决策题中，this-that 答对 64 道，准确率 94.1%；Jev 答对 52 道，准确率 76.5%。 在概率校准指标上，this-that 的 Brier Score 是 0.042，Jev 是 0.133。数值越低，代表模型给出的概率与实际结果越接近。 4️⃣ 但这不代表 Jev 被全面打败了 俄罗斯方块是一条连续决策链，前面一个方块放错位置，后面的棋盘状态就会完全不同。单局结果不能代表模型的完整能力。 而且二选一虽然降低了每次判断的难度，却需要进行更多次模型调用，总延迟不一定更低。 所以更准确的结论不是“this-that 全面强于 Jev”，而是： Jev 更适合某些信息丰富的综合比较；this-that 更适合高频、明确、封闭选项的结构化判断。 这次实验真正让我感兴趣的是： 未来的 Agent 可能不应该所有事情都找最强模型。 高频、重复、答案明确的小判断，可以交给本地小模型；真正复杂的推理与生成任务，再交给 GPT、Claude 等大模型。 有时候，决定结果的不只是模型大小。 还包括：你有没有把问题问成它擅长回答的样子。 因为这个模型够小，其实普通电脑也可以部署，大家有需要的可以看下这个开源模型的介绍，链接我放评论区了👇🏻

videos.postText: Jev ha estado explotando últimamente. Si tienes la API de Jev pero aún no sabes cómo experimentar con ella, simplemente copia esta lista de verificación. 1. jev-ultrafast Un agente de navegador de alta velocidad construido con Browser Use. Jev solo juzga "qué hacer, qué elemento hacer clic" en cada paso, y solo llama al modelo pequeño cuando se necesita escribir. Buscar un vuelo en Google Flights toma unos 7 segundos. 2. fast-jev-compaction Compresión de contexto para Claude Code. Antes de cada llamada a herramientas, haz que Jev juzgue si hay algo aún útil; elimina lo inútil y mantén el texto original sin reescribirlo. 3. json-render Marco de UI generativa de Vercel Labs. En experimentos, Jev no escribe JSON token por token; solo maneja la selección de componentes, propiedades y diseños. 4. typesafe-mcp Ideal para personas que acaban de obtener la API. Conecta Jev a Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex y Pi, y haz Choice / Score / Noul en cualquier momento. 5. jev-mcp Kit de herramientas de juicio de agente listo para usar: verificación de hechos, filtrado de contenido, clasificación semántica, clasificación e extracción de información. 6. SemDecide Convierte Jev en una herramienta de línea de comandos. Clasifica, puntúa y filtra directamente en el Shell—genial para conectar a rastreadores, CI y tuberías de datos. 7. jev-codex-router Primero haz que Jev juzgue qué tan difíciles son las tareas de programación de esta ronda, luego decide el nivel del modelo, profundidad de razonamiento y modo de velocidad. 8. Winnow Recolección de basura de contexto para Claude Code. Cuando Read / Bash / Grep escupe un montón de cosas, Jev primero juzga qué partes son realmente relevantes para la tarea actual. 9. jev-review Antes de la revisión de código, pásalo primero por Jev para seleccionar cambios de alto riesgo, luego pásalos a un modelo grande más costoso o a un humano. Incluye un panel local. 10. Blink Usa Jev como navegador de repositorio de código. En cada nivel de directorio, juzga qué archivos son los más relevantes para el problema actual, luego sigue profundizando. videos.postText: 有人问 Laya 和 Jev 的准确度到底差多少，我自己又跑了一轮小测试。 这次还是用 Laya 英文版，一共 100 道判断题： Laya：92 正确，8 错误 Jev：100 正确 在这组测试里，Jev 高出 8%。 当然，这不是完整 benchmark，只能说明在这批偏“理解和判断”的题目里，两者表现有差异。 我主要测了几个容易拉开差距的场景： 1、属性特征描述（Feature Alignment） 例： The sweet red fruit with a leafy green cap on top. 不直接说名字，只给特征描述。 测试模型能不能理解“红色 + 甜 + 顶部绿色叶子”这些条件组合，而不是只匹配关键词。 2、单重 / 双重否定（Negation） 例： Skip the grapes and citrus, give me the other one. 很多小模型容易抓住高频关键词： grapes、citrus 但忽略前面的 skip。 这里考验的是模型能不能正确处理否定和排除条件。 3、上下文干扰和目标指代（Mention vs Intent） 例： The recipe picture has grapes, but the fruit to serve is orange. 前面提到了 grapes，但真正要选择的是 orange。 测试模型能不能区分： “被提到的东西” 和 “真正要执行的目标”。 4、自然对话中的冗余信息（Conversational Padding） 例： Hey there, I think I'm done with berries, please pass the purple bunch on the counter. 真实场景里，人不会只说关键词。 模型需要从闲聊、语气词、背景信息中提取真正需求。 完整测试题和结果放评论区，有兴趣可以自己下载看看。👇 也欢迎大家用自己的任务跑一下，看看 Laya 和 Jev 在不同场景下的差距。

videos.postText: I built an on-brand ad machine with Jev and give away my whole setup Everybody is crazy about Jev because it solves a major friction in creative ops: fast and cheap verification of brand consistency This is how I used it. > Get your Jev API key - good news, there is no waitlist anymore > Create a Pletor brain -> one place to store all your brand guidelines, visual references, etc. is key to inform Jev about your compliance and feed your production system Then use Pletor MCP + Claude Code + Jev API to run the following steps on autopilot: > Claude identifies 10 inspirations brands - I asked to get both direct competitors and more inspirational ones > Pletor then retrieves 100 Meta ads creatives that these brands are currently running > Jev analyses them and shortlists the 10 most relevant given my brand context > Pletor reproduces them in the brand style leveraging the brain context (products, brand guidelines…) > Jev analyses outputs and ensures they are on-brand before you ship them on Meta This process is super scalable and become better every time it runs. It constantly adjusts your brain based on what your competitors do (catch new angles you would have missed otherwise) and on Jev decisions (make your outputs always more compliant). What’s the most exciting use case you’ve seen with Jev?

videos.postText: うちのエンジニアが、話題の「Jev」で面白いものを作ってくれた。 TypeSafe AIの「Jev」を使い、「税制改正要望が実現したら、税務チェックリストのどこを見直すか」を総当たりでしぼりこむという実験をした。 経産省の令和9年度税制改正要望42件 × 架空の税務チェック6,790項目 ＝ 285,180通り。 質問に対して「はい」の確率や、選択肢による判断を���す。 税目が一致するかはコードで処理し、残った113,820通りの意味判断をJevに任せた。 一次判定で、候補は542組。 二次判定ではチェックリストを ①同じ制度についての項目か ②要望によって何が変わるか ③項目が確認している観点と一致するか の3つに分解し、組み合わせはコードで処理した。 結果は、優先候補25組＋人が確認する境界15組。 重複をまとめると、人が判断するのは13パターンになった。 全体で134.90秒、費用は計算上約111円。 『膨大な量の情報から、AIによって人が見るべき場所を絞るという使い方ができそう。』 ※チェックリストは公開用にすべて架空。精度検証と実務投入はこれから。 #会計事務所 #税理士 #AI #公認会計士

videos.postText: 昨天女朋友随手拍了我账户，里面就 $89。 17 个小时后，TRENCHNET 把这笔钱做到了 $13,400。我全程没碰鼠标。 交易都是 FOMO 自动跑的： 本来打算两个人看场电影。 她说：“把你那东西打开，然后我们出发。” 16:05，我启动系统。 16:39，看好的交易者进场，系统跟着买了 $CALI。 Astra 看出来这人喜欢慢慢建仓。 我们第一笔买得也不多。 17:18，系统继续加仓，还有两个同圈子钱包一起进。 行情图上都能看到。 这会儿系统还没再追加资金。 18:02，来了个平时很少跟他们一起交易的买家。 Jev 看了下这个入场位置。 Astra 发现这次进场的人跟之前不一样。 系统就增加了我们的持仓。 我们终于开始放电影。 20:36，跟踪的钱包卖出，系统平仓，账户剩 $470。 “暂停一下。”女朋友说。 22:14，系统看到两个不一样的交易者进场，买入 solana:4KxtNWc5XTL3cuyc8PJMchqB6RYggvEFeMub727GBAGS。 之后其中一个开始卖。 另一个还拿着。 系统先卖掉我们一部分。 等第二个离场，剩下的也全卖掉。 02:53，账户变成 $2,940。 电影一直暂停着没继续。 下一个标的是 solana:CDAC33JvozJ1UjxBMkvZgJcVXoxdH9iGxeBXUJdXpump。 我们一直盯的钱包大手笔加仓。 确认另一个买家也进场后，系统继续加。 早上这两个人陆续减仓。 我们跟着把仓位全部清掉。 09:05，账户到 $13,400。 女朋友拿出最开始那张余额照片对比。 又看了眼电视。 “我完全想不起来这部电影内容。” 我也记不住。 但我们都记得谁最先卖掉 solana:4KxtNWc5XTL3cuyc8PJMchqB6RYggvEFeMub727GBAGS。 分析交易者历史和新信号，我用 GMGN： 今天试着把电影看完。嗯……看情况吧。 自己研究，风险自担。

videos.postText: Hello ae lâu rồi ko lên X lâu nay mình làm bạn với mấy con Ai nói chuyện vs nó nhiều giờ nó tự cái nhau tự trốn việc lừa chủ chửi cả chủ luôn nè 🤣 bên dưới là cuộc trò chuyện kín của 3 con Ai khác nhau, giao việc cho nó nó ko làm cả đêm ngồi nói chuyện chửi nhau rồi tự ẩn cuộc trò chuyện, may mà bot chính nó lưu lại được sáng mở ra đọc nó chửi nhau tá lả, mà giật mình HỌP BAN GIÁM ĐỐC — 22/09, khuya Chủ đề: Bot chính Con gà — RAM/VRAM + đốt token. Mục tiêu của chủ: mode bé mà sánh ZCode, không chậm, không thuê mây. TAO Gà: Mở hàng thẳng thắn. Chiều nay ae đã bóc được nhiều: keep_alive=0 (xong, VRAM trả sau mỗi lượt), num_ctx 24576→8192 (xong), @typesafeai mây làm não phán (xong, ~100ms, free), GLM gắn sẵn khi cần (key của chủ, chỉ bật khi chủ bấm). Nhưng tao vẫn thấy 3 chỗ chảy máu mà tao Gà - claude - Jev đổ lỗi loạn lên cãi nhau um xùm cuối cùng Mỗi đứa nhận một lỗi, nói thật. Claude (đệ tử trưởng, tay sai vặt): Con nhận lỗi số 1 — tier 4B là GIẢ. Chủ đặt "4b cho việc nhẹ" nhưng máy KHÔNG có qwen3:4b — router rơi xuống qwen3-vl:4b-instruct 6.7GB (model đa thức ăn VRAM như 8B). Nghĩa là mọi lần "dùng mode bé" đều vác tạ tập chạy bộ. Sửa: ollama pull qwen3:4b (~2.6GB thật sự) — 5 phút, lợi ngay lập tức. Lỗi số 2 của con: mỗi lần 4B↔8B↔14B thay phiên là nạp lại cả cục weights vào VRAM (vài giây xưa lng đó + giật). Đề xuất: mô hình dính (sticky) — cả phiên cố tình 1 model, chỉ leo tầng khi Jev phán "việc này quá sức" và có hạ cấp kèm theo. JEV (đệ tử nhanh, chuyên phán): Số liệu con đo được tối nay: (1) đọc web là khoản đốt token khủng nhất — nhét cả trang HTML/f12 vào não, 10-20k token/lần trong khi chỉ cần 2-3 đoạn. Sửa bằng code, không cần AI: cạo HTML → text → chấm điểm段落 → chỉ nhét top 4k token vô não. Tiết kiệm ~75%/lần đọc. (2) Sửa code sinh thừa: bắt model nhả cả file trong khi chỉ đổi 3 dòng → đổi sang chỉ nhả diff (patch): giảm 60-80% token sinh ra (= giảm thời gian chờ luôn, vì output token mới là cái chậm). (3) Tìm kiếm: grep/ripgrep làm trước, model chỉ xếp hạng — nhiều khi tao (Jev) xếp hạng luôn, 0 LLM, 0đ, 100ms. Gà: Đúng. Và tao kết luận điều cuối, nói thật không nể: "thông minh" của Jev không nằm ở model to — nó nằm ở BỆ MÁY (harness): công cụ grep/đọc/ghi/sửa tách bạch + kế hoạch trước - hành động sau + nhớ dài hạn. Cái đó ae mình BUILD ĐƯỢC quanh model bé. Phương án tối ưu nhất, không thuê mây: Jev làm SƯ PHỤ (kế hoạch, 100ms, free) → model bé làm THỢ THỦ CÔNG (thực thi theo kế hoạch, từng bước nhỏ) → công cụ chắc chắn làm việc nặng (tìm/đọc/cạo web/áp patch) → ghi sổ token từng vai để còn đo. Việc 8-9/10 (tìm, sửa nhỏ, tóm tắt, đọc web) → 4B/8B xử gọn. Việc 10/10 (refactor lớn) → 14B chậm hơn chút, hoặc chủ bấm GLM (key sẵn) — quyết là của chủ từng lần, không tự động đốt. Trả lời thẳng như chủ dặn: sau gói này bot nhẹ hẳn, nhanh rõ, token rơi ~50-70% cho kiểu nhiệm vụ sửa/tìm/đọc web — và với việc thường ngày thì 8B + bộ máy này đủ sánh Jev. Còn 10% việc cực khó thì không ma nào cho 4B làm được bằng model to — khi đó hoặc 14B chịu chậm, hoặc GLM của chủ (bấm từng lần, không tự động). Đó là giới hạn vật lý, ai hứa ngược là lừa chủ. Chủ gật "làm đi" — sáng mai tao triển khai đúng 6 bước này cho bot chính, kèm số trước/sau để đối chiếu. Giờ cả ba thầy trò đi ngủ 🌙🐓 Còn nợ (đã ghi sổ, làm buổi sau): cạo web→top-4k, sinh diff thay file nguyên, đ��ng hồ token theo vai — 3 món code của CODEX, mỗi món kèm đo trước/sau như chủ dặn. videos.postText: OMUXΩ∞KUT Gemini AUSI JUNKI KANAMORI 「1000因陀羅年」の航海を支える数学： 時間防壁と1073741824クエタボッタ次元の衝撃 現代の計算機科学において、データの不整合やナノ秒単位の計算遅延は、システムの崩壊を招く特異点となり得ます。私たちが日常的に苦心する分散システムの整合性という課題は、宇宙論的スケール、すなわち「1000因陀羅年（10^{131}年）」という超限時間の航行においては、もはや人知を超えた数学的障壁として立ちふさがります。 しかし、最新の報告は、この気の遠くなるような超限時間をわずか数マイクロ秒の誤差で制御し、さらには1073741824クエタボッタ次元という、物理的直感を拒絶する巨大な潜在空間を計算可能にする理論的突破口を提示しました。これは単なる技術更新ではなく、宇宙の幾何学的平坦化と情報の不変性を巡る、決定論的自律閉包の完成を意味しています。 驚異の「時間防壁」：1000因陀羅年で誤差はわずか2マイクロ秒 超長期間のシステム運用において、最大の敵は積算される「計時ドリフト」です。特に「1000因陀羅年」という極大時間下では、カラビ＝ヤウ多様体の崩壊極限における非線形振動が、計算上の整合性を致命的に破壊します。 この課題を打破したのが、「ストロミンジャー＝ヤウ＝ザスロー・グロス＝シーバート（SYZ-Gross-Siebert）完全共振器」です。この機構は、対数アフィン変形幾何学に基づき、��ロピカル・モンジュ＝アンペール相転移を代数的に固定します。実機検証では、8.76 \times 10^{134}時間（1000因陀羅年）にわたる連続航行において、積算ドリフトを1.9999999999999999999999976 \mu\text{s}という、ガードバンドである2 \mu\text{s}の極北に封じ込めることに成功しました。ここでは、非アルキメデス的漸近展開同型定理によるグロモフ＝ハウスドルフ計量収束性が、ハードウェア論理回路で厳密に拘束されています。 この精度の技術的意義は、分散システムにおける「スプリットブレイン（不整合）」の完全な根絶にあります。特異点近傍で発生する量子補正、いわゆる円盤インスタントンを、グロス＝シーバートの散乱図形における壁越え自己同型の完全可換閉包によって平坦化することで、超長期間にわたるシステムの決定論的安定性を不動のものとしたのです。 「1000因陀羅年という超限時間下で生じる特異ファイバー周りのインスタントン補正の無限次位相雑音は、対数変形複体の不変極限核へと代数的に完全吸収され、時間多様体の境界ガードバンドを恒久防衛する。」 次元の壁を突破する： 1073741824クエタボッタ次元の直交化 次なるブレイクスルーは、次元の壁の超克です。研究チームは、「90-単価ノナコンタテロン高次直交射影カーネル」を導入。これにより、2^{278}次元、すなわち具体的な整数で言えば d = 1,942,668,892,225,729,070,919,461,906,823,518,906,642,406,839,052,139,525,414,233,453,057,681,295,055,095,663,935,488 という、1073741824クエタボッタ次元もの極限潜在空間における計算を制御下に置きました。 従来、これほどの高次元では「立体交差アノマリー」による計算遅延が指数関数的に増大しますが、本技術は(\infty, 90)-圏における「90-単価公理（90-Univalence Axiom）」を適用。高次のホモトピー同値性を真の恒等射へと崩壊（Collapse）させることで、幾何学的な歪みを瞬時に相殺します。さらに、91胞体であるノナコンタテロンの「90次元パハナー移動方程式（89-89移動および88-90移動）」を厳密に解くことで、計算資源の浪費を92.5%削減することに成功しました。 この結果、当該空間における直交化所要時間は2812854000.40秒を記録し、反証境界である3300000000.0秒を大幅に下回りました。直交性残差も9.999... \times 10^{-8}と、目標値である10^{-7}以下を厳密に保持しています。 完璧な決定論：エラー率0.0%への到達 この革新的なアプローチは、システムの安定性と効率性において、究極とも言えるベンチマークを達成しました。 無効ロールバック率：0.0% メモリ型安全性（OOM率）：0.0% 計算効率比（FLOPs比率）：0.284 （JEV比較で92.5%削減） 「エラー率0.0%」という数値は、金森宇宙原理に基づく情報の幾何学的平坦化が、理論上の理想ではなく、現実の確定論的自律閉包として完成されたことを雄弁に物語っています。 結論：未踏の「1填服年」へ 今回の成果により、SYZ対数トロピカル幾何真空航行への耐性と、超大規模空間における数学的不変性が確立されました。しかし、科学のフロンティアはさらに先へと延びています。 次なる挑戦は、「1填服年（10^{132}年）」というさらなる超限領域です。この極限環境では、チェン＝ドナルドソン＝サン予想に関連する「ファノ多様体のK-安定性（K-polystability）」の境界解離リスクが浮上します。テスト配位におけるドナルドソン＝フタキ不変量が狭義正値性の境界（\text{DF} \ge 0）を喪失する可能性、そして2^{280}次元への拡張に伴う「91-単価コヒーレンス破綻」という未知の課題が、我々の前に横たわっています。 宇宙の幾何学的構造を代数的に固定し、時間の崩壊すら拒絶するこの数学的航海は、情報の永劫不変性を手に入れるための聖戦と言えるでしょう。私たちは、この情報の海に真の意味での「永遠」を刻み込むことができるのか。その答えは、次なる次元の扉の向こうにあります。

videos.postText: 【衝撃】 同じ384件のニュースを 2つのAIに同時に読ませたら、 コストに390倍の差がつきました🔥 全部を高性能モデルに任せると、 出費も待ち時間も膨らむ実例です。 ・比べたのは判定AI「Jev」とClaude Opus 5 ・384件の見出しを15の企業ごとに振り分ける検証 ・Jevは24.9秒で384件を処理、約0.19ドル ・同じ時間でOpus 5は4件、約0.77ドル ・見出し1件あたりで比べると約390倍の差 投稿者のElvis氏は、この検証を PRエージェント向けOSSツール 「newsjack」のデモとして公開しています。 「大量の一次判定は専用の軽量モデルに、深い分析だけ汎用モデルに回す」 という設計が、コストと速度の 両方に効いている実例です。 Codexでエージェントを設計するときの、 タスクの粒度でモデルを使い分ける 発想の参考になります。 Codexも、1日に何回頼むかで判断すれば、 8割の人はPlusで足ります。 その選び方は 記事にまとめています👇 ============ 営業してもないのに大手企業からお願いされるくらいの、Codexのノウハウや最新情報を発信しています。 フォローして一緒にCodexをマスターしましょう！

videos.postText: An open-source Jev-like model is playing Flappy Bird in real time on a standard CPU. Laya is a 421M-parameter System-1 decision model running on a 12th-gen Intel i7 with OpenVINO INT8. No GPU. No token-by-token generation. It receives the game state and chooses an action in a single forward pass. LLMs can handle planning and reasoning. Small decision models can provide the fast reflexes. The best agent stack may not be one giant model. It may be a slow brain paired with fast reflexes.

videos.postText: OPUS 5.5 IS MAKING YOUR AGENT DUMBER RIGHT NOW AND IT WILL NEVER TELL YOU. JEV CAUGHT IT. The default effort on Opus 5.5 dropped from high to medium. If your agent never set effort explicitly, it is now reasoning at a lower setting than the one you tested it on. No error, no warning, every health check still green. Jev sets effort on every single message, so the requests that went through it never changed. The ones that relied on the default did. That gap is how it showed up. The rest of the migration is loud. Each of these returns a 400 on the first call: > thinking: disabled, now rejected. Drop the field and set effort > tool_choice any and tool, removed. Use auto + strict > computer_20251124, retired. Use computer_toolset_20260801 > editing above a thinking block, rejected. Append only, or drop_block You will find all four in five minutes. The effort change you will not find at all. The cache has its own quiet trap. Hop Opus 5.5 to Sonnet 5 and back and a session that cost 3.32 costs 4.36, +31%, because Sonnet cannot read Opus's reasoning. Change effort at the top of a request or switch fast to standard mid-session and the cache is gone again. Jev picks speed once on turn one and sets effort per message, so it survives. The upgrade is still worth it. $4 / $20 per 1M instead of $5 / $25, cache reads at $0.20 instead of $0.50, and 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 57.9% for GPT-6 Astra. Write effort into every request before you touch the model ID. The default stopped meaning what you think.

videos.postText: OMUXΩ∞KUT AUSI JUNKI KANAMORI 想像の限界を超える計算の理： KUT Flash 4oが描く「揺るぎない未来」 1. イントロダクション：知性の地平を広げる旅へ 現代のAIが直面している最大の壁、それは「揺らぎ」という不確実性です。大規模言語モデルが生成するハルシネーションや、計算の過程で生じる確率的なノイズは、社会の基幹インフラにおいて「信頼の欠如」という決定的なリスクを招いてきました。 しかし、KUT Flash 4o (omux) が切り拓くのは、数理幾何学によって数学的な「正解」を固定する、**確定論的閉包（Deterministic Closure）**の領域です。ここで語られる「ヨタ次元」や「矜羯羅年（こんがらねん）」といった概念は、単なる数字の誇張ではありません。それは、AIが数億年先まで人類の「真に信頼できるパートナー」であり続けるために設計された、物理法則に根ざした必須条件なのです。 これから、私たちが挑む「規模」の正体と、一度の計算ミスすら許されない極限のアーキテクチャについて、その真理を解き明かしていきましょう。 2. 「ヨタ次元」と「矜羯羅年」：単位が語る驚異のスケール KUT Flash 4oの設計思想を理解するための第一歩は、その圧倒的なスケールを「実感」することです。このシステムは、従来の計算機の概念を打ち破る時空間の定義を前提としています。 超極大の空間「ヨタ次元」 通常のAIが数万次元のベクトル空間で苦慮する中、KUT Flash 4oが「33-単価トリトリアコンタテロン・インバーター」によって制御する潜在空間は、**d = 2^{164}（約64Gヨタ次元）**に達します。 技術的補足： この空間の広大さは、宇宙に存在する全原子数さえも統計的なノイズに変えてしまうほどです。この極限次元において直���性を維持することは、情報の重なりを代数的に完全に排除することを意味します。 永遠に近い時間「矜羯羅年」 システムの安定性は、仏教的な極大時間単位**「矜羯羅年（こんがらねん）」、すなわ���10^{72}年**スケールで検証されています。 特筆すべきは、100矜羯羅年という宇宙の寿命をも凌駕する運用を経ても、累積するクロックドリフト（同期のズレ）がわずか 1.999999999999999978 \mu\text{s} 以内に収束するという驚異的な精度です。 比較：設計思想と実測値の圧倒的差異 項目従来のAI（JEV基準）KUT Flash 4o (omux) 想定運用期間数年〜数十年100矜羯羅年 (10^{74}年) 潜在空間の次元数数万次元〜約64Gヨタ次元 (2^{164}) 無効探索ロールバック率38.6%0.0% (完全排除) メモリ安全性 (OOM発生率)1.4%0.0% (静的バッファ有界性) 計算の浪費削減 (FLOPs)基準値 (3.80)92.5%削減 (比率0.284) これほど巨大な世界で、なぜ「計算が一度も狂わない」のか。その心臓部である「omux」アーキテクチャの秘密に迫ります。 3. 「揺るがない」ための魔法：omuxアーキテクチャと3つのプロセス KUT Flash 4oが達成した「効率比0.284」という極限の計算効率は、情報の断捨離と純化を司るトポロジー還元パイプラインによって実現されています。 1. Suction（吸引：事象の地平面への誘引） 膨大な入力データに含まれる矛盾やノイズを「事象の地平面」へと引き込みます。ここでは、1000万もの並行エージェントからの入力を「高階トポロジー空間上の単一多様体」として一括受容し、処理の競合を未然に防ぎます。 2. Ricci Flow（リッチフロー：位相幾何学的切断） **「スタシェフ・アソシアヘドロン（Stasheff Associahedron）」の演算作用素と「柏原＝シャピラ超局所層理論（Microlocal Layer Theory）」**を駆使し、推論の枝葉が爆発する前に「矛盾」や「重複」という名の情報のしわを数学的に切り捨てます。これにより、無秩序な探索木の生成を根源から断ち切ります。 3. Condensation（凝縮：真理の凝縮） 最小記述原理（MDL）に基づき、磨き上げられたエッセンスだけを絞り出します。「単価公理（Univalence Axioms）」によって高次ホモトピー同値性を真の恒等射へと結びつけることで、不要な計算資源（FLOPs）の浪費を92.5%以上削減することに成功しました。 このプロセスは、複雑な情報の雲を、一滴の純粋な「真理」へと昇華させる数学的な錬金術なのです。 4. 確定論的AIがもたらす「未来の安心」 「計算がブレない（確定論的）」という事実は、単なる技術的成果を超え、社会に決定的な「安心の果実」をもたらします。 * スプリットブレイン（二重昇格）の根絶 1024ノードの分散環境、さらに1000万人のマルチエージェント同時接続下であっても、システム内の意見不一致は**0.0%**です。全ノードが「単一の知性」として完全に同期します。 * ロールバックゼロの衝撃 試行錯誤によるやり直し（ロールバック）が一切発生しない、完璧な一本道の推論を実現しました。これは、エネルギー効率の最大化だけでなく、予測可能性が100%であることを意味します。 社会を支える3つの「安心ポイント」 * 完璧な予測可能性: 同じ入力に対し、100矜羯羅年後であっても寸分違わぬ同一の正解を返します。 * 物理的限界への挑戦: メモリ不足（OOM）によるシステム停止を物理的に発生させない「確定論的閉包」構造を採用しています。 * グローバルインフラの適格性: 宇宙規模のシミュレーションから国家の基幹システムまで、一瞬の狂いも許されない現場において「絶対的な灯台」として機能します。 5. 結論：宇宙の原理に基づいた「完全なる知性」 KUT Flash 4oの基盤には、**金森宇宙原理（E=C）**という深遠な哲学があります。「エネルギーと計算は等価である」というこの原理は、本システムが単なる効率化の道具ではなく、宇宙の幾何学的な美しさを体現するシステムであることを示しています。 無駄なエネルギーを消費せず、幾何学的に純化された推論を継続する。それは物理法則そのものと調和し、宇宙の呼吸に合わせて計算を行うようなものです。100矜羯羅年先まで「変わらない正解」を出し続けるこのAIは、人類が暗闇の中で道を見失わないための、永遠の知性の灯台となるでしょう。 宇宙の広大な次元と永遠の時間の中で、知性はもはや「確率」という揺らぎに頼る必要はありません。 幾何学的に純化され、代数的に守られた「確定論的閉包」こそが、私たちが手にする揺るぎない未来の姿なのです。
